top_five.text: The Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has become the largest in the country's history, exceeding 7,700 confirmed cases and 3,700 deaths across 63 health zones.
Escalating Houthi advances and heavy fighting along Yemen's western coast have displaced over 130,000 people and caused over 110 civilian casualties since early September.
Widespread monsoon flooding affecting more than 470,000 people in Myanmar is exacerbating an ongoing humanitarian emergency driven by conflict and four million internally displaced persons.
Humanitarian conditions in Afghanistan continue to deteriorate, with 28 million people living in poverty as mass population returns and drought strain reduced international assistance.
Renewed intercommunal violence and active fighting across Sudan's Darfur and Kordofan regions have killed at least 13 people and displaced several thousand more.

top_story.quote: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is facing its largest Ebola epidemic on record, with confirmed cases surpassing 7,700 and deaths exceeding 3,700 amidst uncontrolled spread across multiple provinces.

Middle East.headline: Yemen — Mass Displacement and Civilian Casualties Mount Amid Red Sea Offensive
Middle East.body: Escalating hostilities across multiple front lines in Yemen have driven more than 130,000 people from their homes since early September. The UN Refugee Agency warned that internal displacement could reach 230,000, with up to 10,000 refugees fleeing across the Red Sea to Djibouti. The surge follows a rapid Houthi advance along the western coast toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and clashes with Saudi-backed government forces. Fighting has caused hundreds of deaths, including at least 110 civilian casualties. In Mocha, a Saudi-led airstrike reportedly killed six civilians and wounded eight others, while over 150 people were killed in recent two-day clashes.

Africa.headline: DRC — Record Ebola outbreak surpasses 7,700 cases amid regional spread
Africa.body: The World Health Organization and national authorities report that the Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 7,700 confirmed cases and 3,700 deaths, making it the largest in the country's history. The outbreak remains uncontrolled as transmission expands across 63 health zones in provinces including Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Tshopo, Bas-Uele, Haut-Uele, and Sud-Ubangi. Exacerbated by ongoing conflict and displacement, response efforts face treatment shortages and community trust gaps. Humanitarian partners, including MSF and IOM, are establishing new treatment centers in Kisangani and expanding border surveillance. In response to the regional risk, countries including Nigeria have activated heightened health monitoring.

Africa.headline: Sudan — Escalating clashes drive casualties and displacement across Darfur and Kordofan
Africa.body: Escalating violence across Sudan is driving fresh displacement and worsening food insecurity, according to humanitarians. On 19 September, armed intercommunal fighting at Abuja Market in Gereida, South Darfur, left 13 people dead and displaced over 400 individuals. Clashes the same day at Al Borsa Market in El Daein, East Darfur, caused casualties and a partial market closure, alongside reports of fighting in Nyala. Continuous conflict across North and South Kordofan, Blue Nile, and North Darfur has displaced several thousand additional people. The ongoing insecurity severely impacts local commerce and compounds access constraints for vulnerable communities.

Europe.headline: Ukraine/Russia — Zelensky proposes energy ceasefire at UNGA amid warnings of new Russian strikes
Europe.body: On the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed readiness for a mutual halt to energy infrastructure strikes, while warning that Russia is preparing a new mass attack against Ukraine. Zelensky emphasized the urgent need to end the war before winter as civilian conditions deteriorate across the country. Discussions with former US President Donald Trump covered peace negotiation pathways, winter readiness, Patriot missile systems, and potential safeguards for Black Sea grain shipments. French President Emmanuel Macron also called for a moratorium on targeting civilian and energy infrastructure.

Europe.headline: Russia — Ukrainian drone attack targets Kuibyshev oil refinery in Samara
Europe.body: Ukrainian forces launched an overnight drone strike against the Kuibyshev oil refinery in Samara, Russia, approximately 765 kilometers from the Ukrainian border. The attack caused a major fire with heavy smoke at the facility, which has a design capacity of around 7 million tonnes of oil annually. Explosions were also reported in nearby Tolyatti. The strike demonstrates Ukraine's continued capability to target strategic Russian energy infrastructure deep inside Russian territory, even as international diplomatic discussions focus on a potential mutual moratorium on energy sector attacks.
verified_figures: 7 million tonnes annual oil design capacity

Europe.headline: Lithuania — Government prepares civil evacuation plans amid Russian security concerns
Europe.body: Lithuanian officials stated that the country maintains active civil evacuation plans while remaining prepared to defend its territory against potential military threats from Moscow. Officials indicated that the population feels under constant threat from Russia, prompting heightened defense readiness and contingency planning. The announcement underscores persistent security anxieties among Baltic nations bordering Russia, despite the absence of immediate military hostilities on Lithuanian soil.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Floods, Hunger and Disease Pile on Myanmar’s Civil War Misery
Asia-Pacific.body: Wednesday, September 23, 2026 - Isolated and at constant war with itself, Myanmar’s humanitarian crisis is deepening as global challenges far exceed the capacity to respond of a military regime increasingly focused on its own survival. The climate crisis, soaring commodity prices triggered by wars in Europe and the Middle East, plus worldwide cuts in donor aid are all hitting Myanmar hard. The regime’s inability to govern a fragmented and restive country with nearly four million internally displaced people has been exposed to the full since it seized power over five years ago. Asia-Pacific.headline: Sri Lanka Easter bombings: 15 sentenced to hundreds of years in prison each over deadly...
Asia-Pacific.body: Islamic State-inspired bombings of churches and hotels in 2019 was one of the country’s worst ever attacks A court in Sri Lanka has convicted 15 men on terrorist charges for their involvement in the deadly 2019 Easter bombings and sentenced them each to at least 220 years in prison. The terror attacks, which targeted luxury hotels and churches as they held Easter services, left 267 people dead and wounded almost 6000. The bombings, which were inspired by Islamic State (IS), were among the deadliest terror attacks in Sri Lanka’s history and sent shockwaves through the country. Continue reading...

Asia-Pacific.headline: 28 Million in Poverty as Afghanistan Crisis Deepens Amid Returns, Drought and Aid Cuts
Asia-Pacific.body: The Kabul Tribune (KT) — The United Nations says Afghanistan’s humanitarian and economic crisis is worsening, with millions facing deepening poverty due to mass population returns, prolonged drought and declining international assistance. According to a new report by the United Nations Development Programme, an estimated 28 million people were living in poverty in Afghanistan in 2025. The situation has been compounded by the return of approximately 2.9 million Afghans during the year, pushing an additional 1.4 million people into hardship. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: DRC — Ebola Outbreak Expands Across Multiple Provinces
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is scaling up emergency capacity in the Democratic Republic of the Congo as an Ebola outbreak spreads across several provinces. MSF established a new 22-bed treatment centre in Kisangani, Tshopo province, to manage cases spreading from Ituri province. Separately, Sud-Ubangi province recorded its first confirmed Ebola case, involving a Bundibugyo virus patient who died after traveling from South Kivu. Response operations face difficulties due to logistical shortages, strained facilities, and gaps in community trust. In response to the regional health threat, Nigeria's public health agency has activated precautionary monitoring and enhanced travel surveillance.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: South Africa — Confirmed Mpox Cases Rise to 22
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: South Africa’s Department of Health announced that laboratory-confirmed mpox cases in the country have increased from 18 to 22. The additional cases include a 47-year-old male from Cape Town who had traveled to Spain earlier in the month, whose status was reclassified to confirmed following laboratory verification from Spanish health authorities. Health officials have renewed calls for public vigilance and are maintaining surveillance measures to monitor potential ongoing transmission.
